title: Sherwin Gatchalian: US wants PH to address Pax Silica issues first
summary: Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian said US Secretary of State Marco Rubio wants the Philippines to address concerns surrounding the Pax Silica initiative before moving forward with the agreement.

blocks.text: Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian said US Secretary of State Marco Rubio wants the Philippines to address concerns surrounding the Pax Silica initiative before moving forward with the agreement.
Gatchalian said Rubio told him during US President Donald Trump's state visit to the Philippines that the government should be given enough time to resolve issues surrounding the initiative.

“He said he knows there are many issues and problems. We should not rush things and should give the Philippine government time to address these concerns,” Gatchalian said in an interview with Super Radyo dzBB on Sunday.
Gatchalian said the United States was monitoring the situation and recognized the need to resolve concerns involving both Pax Silica and the Luzon Economic Corridor before proceeding.
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. recently hosted Trump for a bilateral meeting and a state luncheon at Malacañang. Rubio accompanied Trump during the visit and also met with Gatchalian.

Pax Silica is a US-led economic security initiative aimed at building a global supply chain for artificial intelligence and the semiconductor industry. The Philippines is among the 24 countries that have signed on to the initiative.

As part of the initiative, a 1,600-hectare AI-focused industrial hub is being eyed in New Clark City, Tarlac. The proposed development is expected to process critical minerals and manufacture high-tech components for AI and semiconductor industries.
The project is expected to generate jobs and boost government revenues and tax collections through AI processing, chip manufacturing and mining.
However, environmental groups and other stakeholders have raised concerns about the initiative's potential environmental impact and the displacement of local communities.— MCG, GMA News
